title: C standard library overview and headers
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its C rules.
Trace the example and identify data or control flow.
Recognize common failure and safety cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: The C standard library provides facilities for input/output, strings, memory allocation, mathematics, character handling, time, diagnostics and other common tasks. Headers declare interfaces; the implementation supplies the corresponding library definitions.
understand.whyItMatters: Using standard facilities improves portability and reduces the need to write error-prone replacements, provided the program follows their contracts.
understand.analogy: Treat each resource and operation as having a clear contract, valid lifetime and failure path.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, compiler or library specifications.

explain.narrative:
The C standard library provides facilities for input/output, strings, memory allocation, mathematics, character handling, time, diagnostics and other common tasks. Headers declare interfaces; the implementation supplies the corresponding library definitions.

Check object bounds, lifetimes, arithmetic limits and all relevant return values. Compile with warnings enabled and test both normal and failure paths.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: stdio.h declares printf and string.h declares strlen. The program uses standard library interfaces instead of implementing output and string length manually.

practise.guidedTask: Match each header to a common facility it declares.
practise.independentTask: Create a small program that uses stdio.h, string.h and ctype.h, explaining the role of each header.
hints: A header provides declarations and macros; it is not itself a separately compiled program.
Include the standard header that declares each library function you use.
Check the C version and implementation support for facilities you depend on.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable way to protect correctness?
options: Validate preconditions, bounds and failure results.
Ignore the type and lifetime rules.
questions.answer: Validate preconditions, bounds and failure results.
questions.explanation: C requires explicit handling of object validity and operation failures.

questions.prompt: How should the example be checked?
options: Compile with warnings and test expected and failure cases.
Ignore diagnostics and test only once.
questions.answer: Compile with warnings and test expected and failure cases.
questions.explanation: Warnings and targeted tests provide evidence for correctness.
